FROM IMAGE TO OBJECT

A little lattice. A complete print set.

Choose an image, set the panel dimensions and your printer bed, then export. The conversion runs entirely on your Mac.

Modular or fused?

Modular prints a lattice frame with support ledges and separate patterned inserts. Inserts are packed by filament color. Fused unions the motifs and grid into one solid object per bed-sized tile for a single filament.

Make the image readable

Tone mapping uses denser motifs for darker image areas. Texture mapping follows local variation. Constant motif mode preserves the image through filament colors. Strong silhouettes and simple backgrounds work best. Smaller triangles give more detail.

A complete export

The ZIP includes all frame/panel STLs, every insert at the required quantity, optional backing, a fit-test coupon for modular mode, a numbered assembly SVG, print-plate maps, a JSON manifest, and printing instructions. STL has no color; assign the listed filaments in your slicer.

Fit and assembly

Print the fit-test first. Clearance is per side. Inserts drop onto a ledge and can be glued; they are not snap locks. Split frames have butt seams that need alignment and adhesive. All pieces print flat with supports off. Test your printer tolerances before printing the full set.

Edit individual cells

Open Cell map, click a cell, and choose its motif or filament. Save a project to retain the image, settings and edits. If you change the panel size, grid direction or triangle edge, cell IDs change and existing edits are cleared.

References

Inspired by Julius Ang’s printable pattern generator and Hampus Udd’s image-to-triangular-pattern approach. Geometry uses the bundled Manifold kernel. All app source and build instructions are included in the distribution.

macOS 12 or newer · Intel and Apple Silicon · unsigned local build
